It solves high compilation overhead and poor runtime performance in dynamic dispatch scenarios common in differentiable rendering by generating indirect calls to separate subroutines rather than merging functions into a single large kernel body or committing loop state to memory at every iteration [S1].

Furthermore, the source notes that Dr.Jit exploits redundancy in dynamic dispatch to reduce backend compilation time, addressing the 'high compilation overhead' mentioned in the claim. The specific mechanisms described in the claim (indirect calls vs. merging functions/committing state) are directly cited in the text.
